---
title: "Multirates inference"
---

## title: "Variational vs MCMC inference"

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(PEPI)
library(cmdstanr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

PEPI's unified model (`inst/multirates_positive_s.stan`) jointly infers, from
multi-sample VAF-derived CCF data collected at several sampling times:

- the base growth rate `lambda_n` and epigenetic fitness `s_epi` of a
  wild-type ("wt") background population switching between "-" and "+"
  epistates at rates `omega_n_wt`/`omega_p_wt`;
- any number of **driver** clades (their own fitness `s_driver` and switch
  rates), **driver-only** clades confined to a single epistate
  (`driver_n`/`driver_p`), and **driver+clade** combos (`dc`, a driver
  acquisition followed by a further epimutation-switch event); and
- **wt-background clades** (`clades_wt`), sub-lineages of the wt population
  tracked for their own epistate composition.

## Load data and fit both ways

Stan's own sampler console output is suppressed below for readability - it
normally includes informational messages about rejected initial values
during warmup, which are expected and not a sign of a problem here.

```{r, results = "hide", message = FALSE}

# Load the example datasets included with the package.
data("counts")
data("muts")
data("forest")
data("mu")

# Extract the two sampling times from the counts table.
sampling_times = c(
  counts$sampling_time_1 %>% unique(),
  counts$sampling_time_2 %>% unique()
)

# Estimate the fraction of cells in each epistate at each sampling time
# from the phylogenetic forest.
ccf = forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample)) %>% group_by(epistate,sample) %>%
  summarize(n = length(cell_id)) %>% group_by(sample) %>% mutate(n = n/sum(n))

# Estimate the total population size at the two sampling times.
z1 = counts %>% filter(time == sampling_times[1]) %>%
  group_by(epistate,mutant) %>% summarize(count = max(count)) %>%
  pull(count) %>% unique() %>% sum()

z2 = counts %>% filter(time == sampling_times[2]) %>%
  group_by(epistate,mutant) %>% summarize(count = max(count)) %>%
  pull(count) %>% unique() %>% sum()

set.seed(31)

# Add lognormal noise
z1 = exp(rnorm(n = 1,mean = log(z1),sd = 0.2))
z2 = exp(rnorm(n = 1,mean = log(z2),sd = 0.2))

zminus = c(z1,z2)*(ccf %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))
zplus = c(z1,z2)*(ccf %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))

# Identify the driver lineage and reconstruct its branch in the forest.
driver_id = forest %>% filter(mutant == "B") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()

get_branch = function(forest,cell_id,stop_id){
  s = cell_id
  branch = s
  while(s > stop_id){
    s = forest %>% dplyr::filter(cell_id == s) %>% pull(ancestor)
    if(s > stop_id){branch = c(branch,s)}
  }
  return(branch)
}

driver_branch = get_branch(forest,cell_id = driver_id,stop_id = 0)

# Estimate the number of mutations associated with the driver branch
m_driver_branch = muts %>%
  filter(first_cell_id %in% driver_branch) %>% nrow()

# Add binomial noise
m_driver = rnbinom(n = 1,mu = m_driver_branch,size = 100)

# Estimate the driver CCF from the four VAF measurements.
ccf_dr = 2*(muts %>% filter(first_cell_id %in% driver_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Sampling_1_N.VAF,Sampling_1_P.VAF,
    Sampling_2_N.VAF,Sampling_2_P.VAF
  ) %>%
  reshape2::melt() %>%
  group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>% pull(v))

# Build the driver CCF table.
ccf_driver = tibble(
  driver_id = "B",
  time = rep(sampling_times, each = 2),
  epistate = rep(c("-","+"), 2),
  ccf = c(
    ccf_dr[1],
    ccf_dr[3],
    ccf_dr[2],
    ccf_dr[4]
  )
)

# The wild-type CCF is the complement of the driver CCF.
ccf_wt = tibble(
  time = rep(sampling_times, each = 2),
  epistate = rep(c("-","+"), 2),
  ccf = c(
    1 - ccf_dr[1],
    1 - ccf_dr[3],
    1 - ccf_dr[2],
    1 - ccf_dr[4]
  )
)

# Assemble the tables required by init_multirates().
tables = list(
  population_sizes = tibble(
    time = sampling_times,
    type = "sampling",
    zminus = zminus,
    zplus = zplus
  ),

  wt_ccf = ccf_wt,

  driver_muts = tibble(
    driver_id = "B",
    m_driver = m_driver,
    ms_driver = -0.8,
    sigma_driver = 0.9,
    alpha_n_driver = 1.5,
    beta_n_driver = 4,
    alpha_p_driver = 0.3,
    beta_p_driver = 6
  ),

  driver_ccf = ccf_driver
)

# Fit the same model with ADVI and with full NUTS sampling.
fit_args = list(
  cmdstan_path = cmdstanr::cmdstan_path(),
  seed = 31,
  mu = mu$mean,
  l = 51e06,
  t_min = -20,
  ms_epi = -0.8,
  sigma_epi = 0.9,
  alpha_lambda = 10,
  beta_lambda = 10,
  alpha_n_wt = 1,
  beta_n_wt = 1e4,
  alpha_p_wt = 0.2,
  beta_p_wt = 10,
  min_kappa = 3000,
  max_kappa = 5000,
  min_sigma_count = 0.05,
  max_sigma_count = 0.15,
  include_poisson = 1,
  include_trunk = 0
)
```

`fit_multirates()` supports full Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (NUTS). It is
  asymptotically exact, and comes with the convergence
  diagnostics covered in `vignette("Convergence_diagnostics")` (R-hat,
  effective sample size, divergences, ...)

```{r, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
x = init_multirates(tables, m_trunk = 0)
x = do.call(
  fit_multirates,
  c(list(x = x, chains = 4, ndraws = 1000), fit_args)
)

```


## Extract the posterior

```{r}

x = get_posterior_multirates(x)
x$posterior$multirates

```

## Predicted vs observed

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
plot_counts_multirates(x)
```

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
plot_fractions(x)
```

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
plot_ccf(x)
```

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
plot_mutations(x)
```

## Posterior vs prior, and ground-truth recovery

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}

plot_inference(x, params = c("lambda_n","s_epi","s_driver","omega_p_wt","omega_n_driver","omega_p_driver")) +
  geom_vline(
    data = data.frame(
      facet = c("lambda_n","s_epi","s_driver","omega_p_wt","omega_n_driver","omega_p_driver"),
      truth = c(1.0, 0.5, 0.3, 8e-03, 0.3, 4e-02)
    ),
    aes(xintercept = truth), linetype = "dashed", color = "red"
  )

```

The dashed red lines mark the ground-truth values used to simulate the data;
posterior histograms should bracket them.
